summary: Shoko Kanaoka (1930–1987) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He taught Stephan Marcus Salzberg and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1987, 2000).
Shoko Miyabayashi (1932–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University from circa 1951 to 1958 and later held a post there from circa 1974 to 2003.

Shoko Takeuchi (1910–1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (attested 1987–1995, 2009) and taught Koyo Shimizu, Toshihide Mori, and Shodo Fujita.

Shoko Watanabe (1907–1977) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) and under Ernst Leumann, later holding posts at Kyushu University (~1947–1953), Toyo University (~1958–1976), and Taisho University.

Shoku Bando (b. 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg, holding posts in 1987 at Abhidharma Kenkyūjo, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoren Ihara is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1977) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998), and taught Kunio Harikai and Hiromasa Tosaki.

Shoryu Katsura (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto, and held professorships at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara (1907–1975) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University, Horyu-ji, and under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki, later holding posts at Otani University, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima (1928–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies. He was a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaii and served as Dean of Academic Affairs and later Professor Emeritus at Taisho University (attested 1983–2014).

Shoshin Kuwayama (b. 1938) works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1961) and later served there as assistant professor (~1973–1989).

Shoson Miyamoto (1893–1983) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University (~1954–1973), and Waseda University (~1954–1964).

Shou-chien Shih (b. 1951) works in history, archaeology, and sinology. He served as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004) and as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002), teaching Pei-jung Wu.

Shoyu Hanayama (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at Musashino University (~1970–1995) and chairperson of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (~1985–1995).

Shozen Kumoi (1915–2017) studied at Otani University (~1938–1941) and researched Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Otani University (1948–1981, emeritus ~1986), Kyoto University (1971–1973), and Bukkyo University (1982).
Shri Krishna Saksena is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who taught John M. Koller. He held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaii (both attested 2016).

Shridhar Ramkrishna Bhandarkar (b. 1859) was an Indologist. He served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College, and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held a post at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (1881–1967) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak (~1902–1904). He served as General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1920–1943) and Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (attested 1929).
Shrivatsa Goswami (b. 1950) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University. He held a post at the Vrindaban Research Institute (attested 1994).

Shu-chen Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen C. Lang, also serving there as a teaching assistant in 1996.
